summary: Provides a framework for developing protocol extensions so GMPLS and PCE can control Optical Transport Networks as specified in ITU-T G.709 (2012 edition). It is a framework document, with the detailed protocol work left to other documents.

eli5.summary: A plan for how network computers should steer light-based phone-company cables.

subtitle: What GMPLS and PCE need to change to control the newer G.709 optical transport networks.

tldr.problem: The 2012 revision of ITU-T G.709 added new containers, a second tributary slot size and ODUflex, which the earlier GMPLS signaling for OTN (RFC 4328) cannot control.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC reviews how OTN works from a control-plane view and lists what signaling, routing, link management, PCE and management protocols would need to support.
tldr.outcome: It is a framework only: it states requirements and leaves the actual protocol extensions to other documents.

today: RFC 7062 is an Informational framework and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It sets out requirements; the protocol extensions themselves are left to other documents.

sections.title: Why OTN Needs a New Framework
sections.content:
Optical Transport Networks (OTNs) are described as a mainstream layer 1 technology for transport networks. Operators want a GMPLS control plane on them for benefits such as better resiliency and more efficient use of resources.

RFC 4328 gave basic GMPLS control of OTN based on the 2001 revision of ITU-T G.709. The 2012 revision adds several multiplexing structures, two types of tributary slots (1.25 Gbps and 2.5 Gbps) and the ODUflex container. This document reviews those changes, explains why and how the RFC 4328 mechanisms should be updated, and discusses the Path Computation Element (PCE).

For control purposes the OTN is seen as an ODU layer and a wavelength (OCh) layer. This document covers the ODU layer; the wavelength layer is out of scope and is covered by RFC 6163.
sections.eli5: The light-cable system got upgrades, so the old instructions for steering it are out of date. This paper explains what has to be updated.

sections.title: How G.709 OTN Is Built
sections.content:
Client signals are mapped into ODUj containers. These are multiplexed onto an OTU/OCh, and the OTU/OCh signals are combined in the OMS using Wavelength Division Multiplexing. The values of j defined in G.709 (2012) are 0, 1, 2, 2e, 3, 4 and flex. ODUflex can have any bit rate with a tolerance of +/-100 ppm.

A lower-order ODUj is either mapped directly into an OTUk (when j equals k) or multiplexed into a higher-order ODUk (k greater than j) by occupying tributary slots. The number of slots used depends on both j and k. For example, an ODU2e uses 9 slots in an OTU3 but only 8 in an OTU4.

A node with 1.25 Gbps slots must fall back to 2.5 Gbps slots when connected to legacy equipment; this is signalled in band by the payload type. The in-band MSI information, with one entry per slot holding a payload type and a Tributary Port Number (TPN), lets the far end demultiplex correctly. If the received MSI differs from the expected one, traffic is dropped and a payload mismatch alarm is raised.
sections.eli5: Think of a truck with many small boxes of different sizes. Small shipments get packed into the boxes, and a label on each box tells the receiver what is inside.

sections.title: Connection Management of ODU Paths
sections.content:
In the newer ITU-T model the ODU is a single-layer network with the bit rate as a parameter of links and connections. Nodes and links can then be seen as one topology of resources that can provide ODUj connections whatever the value of j.

The RFC considers two control-plane views. In the first, ODU links join adjacent optical digital cross connects (ODXCs). A request for a connection selects a path with enough free tributary slots and the lowest cost, and signaling then tells each transit node which slots to use. In the second, the ODU layer sits above wavelength-switching nodes such as ROADMs or OXCs, forming a multi-layer network. The operator may hide the OCh topology as a cloud or make it visible. A higher-order ODU or OCh connection then appears at the ODU level as a Forwarding Adjacency.
sections.eli5: Planning a route means finding roads with enough free space, then telling every stop along the way which spots to use.

sections.title: What GMPLS and PCE Must Support
sections.content:
Section 5 is the heart of the framework: a set of requirements for extending the existing protocols.

  • Signaling: carry the new signal types (ODU0, ODU2e, ODU4, ODUflex) with the bit rate for ODUflex; identify the slot granularity; define a new label format for slot allocation; carry TPN information; support virtual concatenation with LCAS; and support hitless adjustment of ODUflex (GFP).
  • Routing: a new Switching Capability for G.709 ODU switching, advertising multiplexing capability, accurate bandwidth for any ODU and ODUflex, terminating versus switching capability, slot granularity, up to 8 priority levels as in RFC 4202, link bundling and resizable ODUflex.
  • Link management: the two ends of a link should correlate slot granularity and the supported LO ODU types through LMP.
  • PCE: the PCE communication protocol should be extended to carry the new signal types and variable bandwidth.

The LSP hierarchy can also be used inside the ODU layer, for example to tunnel new services through legacy ODU1, ODU2 and ODU3 containers so that not every node must be upgraded at once.
sections.eli5: The steering computers need to learn about the new box sizes, advertise what they can carry, and agree with their neighbours on which box size to use.

sections.title: Backward Compatibility
sections.content:
Networks may mix legacy nodes that run the RFC 4328 control plane with nodes that support G.709 (2012). Compatibility only matters for ODU1, ODU2 and ODU3 connections, since those are the only types the legacy OTN supports. The RFC lists options: a new node supports only the new procedures, in which case the two kinds of node cannot jointly control an LSP, or a new node supports both control planes and chooses between them based on the Switching Capability advertised in routing or the Switching Type in received signaling.

In the data plane, a node with 1.25 Gbps slots can interwork with a 2.5 Gbps node by combining slots. In the RFC's example on an ODU2 link, slots TS#i and TS#i+4 are combined, and the label sent to the legacy node indicates TS#i at 2.5 Gbps granularity. The control plane must support this combination.
sections.eli5: When old and new equipment meet, the new one agrees to talk the old way, like switching to a simpler language so both can understand.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Using control-plane protocols for signaling, routing and path computation exposes an OTN to attacks on those protocols. The RFC says this risk is no greater than that of the existing OTN control plane defined by RFC 4203 and RFC 4328.

It adds that the data communication network for the control protocols is likely to be in the in-fiber overhead, which together with access lists at the network edges is a significant security feature. RFC 5920 gives an overview of GMPLS control-plane vulnerabilities and protections.
sections.eli5: Steering computers could be attacked, but no more than before, and the private control channel inside the cable helps keep strangers out.
